candidates.buyer: SLBFE-licensed foreign employment agencies (owner-run, many with branch offices)
candidates.existing: None seen in the search. SLBFE itself runs online portals (services.slbfe.lk, applications.slbfe.lk) for login, payment and the licensee list. Whether agencies use a case-management or compliance product is unchecked.
candidates.name: Overseas employment agency licence-renewal and SLBFE reporting pack
candidates.trigger: SLBFE Act: licence valid 1 year; renewal application 30 days before expiry; SLBFE reviews prior-year performance (minimum 60 recruits), inspects records, and requires conciliation, investigation, legal, trafficking and finance (cess) reports, ABCD reports, remittance updates and branch records in a prescribed format.
candidates.unchecked: Number of licensed agencies; whether the SLBFE portal already accepts the renewal and the periodic reports; existing agency ERP or CRM vendors. The Sinhala/English competitor search was not run (budget exhausted).

candidates.buyer: Cattle, goat, buffalo and pig traders and transporters
candidates.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
candidates.existing: None seen. Permits appear to be paper and office-based.
candidates.known_note: Not close to a known idea.
candidates.name: Livestock movement permit and health-certificate tracker for cattle and goat traders
candidates.trigger: Animals Act No. 29 of 1958 and the DAPH guidelines under the 26 Nov 2009 gazette: District/Divisional Secretary transport permit (valid 2 weeks), government vet health certificate, cattle voucher, ear tags, per-animal fees; the African swine fever gazette of Nov 2024 requires a vet report for pigs.
candidates.unchecked: Whether DAPH or districts have digitised permits; trader numbers; how strictly this is enforced.

candidates.trigger: Motor Traffic Act Part VIIA and Regulations No. 1 of 2015 (school categories A/B/C, licensed instructors, 2021 amendment). Registration restarted in 2024 and made compulsory. Reported cap of 40 novice drivers per month and a planned new gazette (unconfirmed).
candidates.unchecked: The registration deadline, the monthly reporting duty, and whether the planned gazette was issued. A one-off registration helper has low frequency.

Not enacted; stakeholder consultations in Oct 2026.
candidates.unchecked: Whether and when the bill is passed; the court outcome on the 2024 directive; buyers are small unpaid volunteers. The Sinhala competitor search was not run.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Registration of Domestic Servants Ordinance only applies where brought into force by gazette order; no active national register found. ILO launched a voluntary Standard Employment Contract for live-in and live-out domestic workers on 11 Sep 2025. Proposed Employment Act not confirmed enacted. No mandatory recurring duty found.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: One search returned no Sri Lankan sources. No national scrap-metal licensing regime found. Unverified whether local-authority or CEA licences apply.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Pawnbrokers Ordinance No. 13 of 1942 (licence from Divisional Secretary, security deposit). Provincial statutes now set fees and deposits: Western Province registration Rs 50,000 plus annual Rs 25,000; North Western gazette (March 2025) requires a Rs 200,000 security deposit. Fragmented by province. The gazette fetch returned 503, so details are from search snippets. No second-hand dealer regime found.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: NGJA requires jewellers to issue a certificate to customers (carat/PPT, trademark, price) under the Assaying and Hallmarking Regulations; licence cancellation for non-compliance (Sunday Times, Dec 2023, per search snippet). No mandatory-hallmark gazette for 2025 found. Related to K05 but a different buyer group (retail jewellers).

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No Sri Lankan dismantler or end-of-life vehicle regime found. DMT removes vehicles with no revenue licence for 5 years from its system (May 2023). Nothing mandatory for parts dealers.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Animals Act 1958: transport permit from District/Divisional Secretary, valid 2 weeks, needs a government vet health certificate, ear tags Rs 20/animal, Rs 50/animal fee. DAPH guidelines are from a 2009 gazette. African swine fever movement relaxation from 4 Nov 2024; current status unknown.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Butchers Ordinance: annual or temporary licence from the local authority. Private slaughterhouses also need an Environmental Protection Licence and Factories Ordinance registration. Licences are issued per local authority, so fragmented. No central register.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No search spent (budget used on categories with clearer regulators). Unverified.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Veterinary Surgeons and Practitioners Act No. 46 of 1956: individual registration with the Veterinary Council. No premises licensing or medicine-seller register found. Low volume of buyers.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Water Resources Board: 2017 report says tube well builders must register; 2017 gazette requires WRB supervision of groundwater use for certain projects. Proposed annual well permit (Rs 7,500-15,000) under WRB Act amendments, enactment unconfirmed. No official WRB page found.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: CEA scheduled waste licence (Regulations No. 1 of 2008, Schedule VIII) covers collect/transport/store/recycle. No result on septage haulers. Unverified.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Factories Ordinance: 2019 regulations (boiler registration, examination certificates, accredited inspectors reporting to the Chief Factory Inspecting Engineer) presented to Parliament; final gazette status unconfirmed. Lift examination under the 1960 regulations. Owners are mainly factories.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Community-based organisations (3,400+ rural schemes) are registered with the Department of National Community Water Supply. CBOs have no clear legal mandate and often lack treatment and quality control. No tariff or regulator duty found.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Control of Pesticides Act 1980: Registrar licenses importers, formulators and sellers. Agro-dealers must hold NVQ Level 4 (provisional licence, full certification after 4 years' experience; per 2025 PlantwisePlus blog). Fertiliser dealer rules not found.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: SLBFE licensed foreign employment agencies: annual renewal (apply 30 days before expiry), Rs 5m bank guarantee, minimum 60 recruits/year, internal reports (conciliation, investigation, legal, trafficking, finance/cess), ABCD reports, remittance updates, branch records, inspections. Fee revised July 2023.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No search spent (budget). Unverified.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: NGO Secretariat Dec 2024 directive requires all NGOs to register with it; Supreme Court petition filed Jan 2025 (outcome not found). Draft NGO (Registration and Supervision) Bill 2026 would replace the 1980 VSSO Act, with portal registration, annual action plans and quarterly progress reports, still in consultation (Oct 2026). Halal certification is voluntary, run by private certifiers (ACJU, HAC); no mandatory register.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: NTC issues private bus route permits (tender); 2026 gazette sets permit transfer rules (written or electronic application, 25% cap per route). School service permits under a 2013 gazette; 2023 gazette fee schedule (annual registration Rs 10,000 bus, Rs 3,000 van, unverified applicability). K13 already covers three-wheelers. No digital ticketing mandate found.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Money changers: Central Bank permits under Foreign Exchange Act No. 12 of 2017; only 59 permits in 2025 plus 6 finance companies and 12 hotels, so a tiny buyer pool. Street vendors and market traders not searched.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Driving schools: about 1,500 schools, 800 registered, 700 not; registration restarted July 2024; Motor Traffic Regulations No. 1 of 2015 (A/B/C categories, licensed instructors, 2021 amendment, 40-novice monthly cap reported). Day care: provincial statutes (Southern 2019, Uva 2014) plus 2019 national guidelines, no uniform register. Food: labelling and trans-fat regulations in force from 1 July 2026. Tattoo studios and hunting outfitters not applicable or not found.
